newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares close firmer, buoyed by lower rates.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares close firmer, buoyed by lower rates.

text.p: New Zealand shares closed firmer on reasonable volumes on Wednesday as lower wholesale interest rates freed up cash for investment in equities, brokers said.
"We were positive right from the outset in light of the rally in 90-day bank bills and bonds yesterday," said Tim Koller at Merrill Lynch.
The NZSE-40 Capital closed 10.34 points firmer at 2,253.55, with Carter Holt Harvey up five at NZ$3.13 and Brierley up two at $1.29.
Brokers said said the positive sentiment was sparked by Tuesday's lower-than-expected March quarter core inflation data, but also by U.S. asset strength.
"Overnight the U.S. got a boost from a better-than-expected CPI (Consumer Price Index) number, which allowed their bonds to rally and their equities to surge," Koller said.
The Dow closed 135.26 points stronger at 6,587.16.

Fletcher Energy continued its fine recent run, ending eight cents firmer at $4.24 after a 16 cent rise on Tuesday. Brokers said they had heard Energy was conducting a road show in the United States which may be attracting new
investors, but they also noted a rise in the oil price.

Brokers said a 2.4 perent fall in February retail trade data was well below market expectations and contributed to the picture of a slowing economy. However, the drop in retail sales was something of a double-edged sword for equities.

"The slower economy will translate into lower earnings for companies, but it does show that the economy is still slowing down and that makes it more likely that rates will be allowed to ease," Koller said.
